doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Early professional days with a valve trombone and soap
summary: Ory recalls patching his valve trombone with soap, earning $4 a week, and being happy despite poverty.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. I had me an old valve trombone, you know. And I had some in the holes, and I used to put soap in it. I had $4 a week. And as long as the soap didn't get damp, you know, I was going. I was all right. You get damp, you don't want bubbles. Bubbles, yeah. Told the guys, go ahead, I'll catch up where I put some more soap. Yeah, I was the first guy of a blue bubble. It was pretty tough, but we had lots of fun.
Not much money, but lots of fun, wasn't it, huh? Oh, yeah. I wasn't worried about money. You wake up broke, whistling, and just happy. Now, if you wake up broke, boy, you want to cry. 된 stuff
